title: Dynamic Arrays
concept: Array whose size is determined at runtime (user input size)

steps.title: Include header files
steps.explanation:
Uses output and dynamic memory functions, including `stdio.h` and `stdlib.h`.

This lesson covers dynamic arrays whose size is determined at runtime.

steps.title: Start main function
steps.explanation:
The main frame is created.

Unlike static arrays, dynamic arrays are allocated on the heap at runtime size.

steps.title: Size variable declaration
steps.explanation:
Declare a `size` variable to contain the length of the array.

This value will be used later to calculate malloc size.

steps.title: input prompt output
steps.explanation: Prints an array length input guide.

steps.title: Set size (input simulation)
steps.explanation:
In the example, we set the length to `size = 5`.

In practice, this is where user input is received.

steps.title: Dynamic memory allocation (malloc)
steps.explanation:
Create a heap array to store `size` integers with `malloc(sizeof(int) * size)`.

Store the returned starting address in the pointer `arr` and use it like an array.

steps.title: Initializing and printing an array with a for loop
steps.explanation:
Fill in the value using the `arr[i]` syntax and print it.

The indexing approach for dynamic arrays is the same as for static arrays.

steps.title: free memory
steps.explanation:
Return the entire dynamic array at once with `free(arr)`.

The dynamic array pattern is allocate, then use, and finally free.

quiz.question: What function do you use when you want to increase the size of a dynamic array?
quiz.explanation: The `realloc(ptr, new_size)` function adjusts the memory size while maintaining existing data (or moves if there is no space).

misconceptions.wrong: Dynamic arrays must be freed multiple times.
misconceptions.correct: You only need to do it once.
misconceptions.why: Since we borrowed the whole thing by calling `malloc` once, we call `free` only once to return the whole thing.

keyTakeaway: If you don’t know the size, use `malloc`. It can be easily handled by using the array syntax ([]) as is.
